title: Fascia's role in chronic pain: disorders, mechanisms, and treatments
question: What does current research say about the role of fascia in chronic pain — the disorders and mechanisms that implicate fascia, and the treatments that target it?

sub_questions.text: By what mechanisms is fascia thought to contribute to chronic pain (innervation and nociception, inflammation/fibrosis, mechanotransduction, fascial densification/stiffness, sensitization)?

Which chronic pain conditions and fascia disorders are most strongly linked to fascial dysfunction (e.g. chronic low back pain, myofascial pain syndrome, fibromyalgia, plantar fasciitis, neck/shoulder pain)?

What fascia-targeting treatments are used for chronic pain and what does the evidence say about their efficacy (manual/myofascial release, fascial manipulation, dry needling, hydrodissection, acupuncture, extracorporeal shockwave, exercise)?
How is fascial dysfunction measured or imaged in research (ultrasound elastography, gliding/shear-strain imaging, biopsy), and how strong is the objective evidence linking these measures to pain?
What are the active research directions, controversies, and open questions in the fascia–chronic-pain field?

scope.recency: prefer sources < 7 years old, but include foundational/landmark work where relevant
scope.notes: Deep-research (non-exhaustive) synthesis to get up to speed on the state of fascia + chronic pain research. Emphasis on peer-reviewed literature; flag where evidence is preliminary or contested.
